chunks: When you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down.
And let a scribe write it between you with justice.
And no scribe should refuse to write as Allah has taught him; so let him write.
And let the one upon whom is the debt dictate, and let him fear Allah his Lord, and not leave out anything of it.
If the one upon whom is the debt is deficient of mind or weak, or is unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate with justice.

And call to witness two witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men [available], then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses, so that if one of the two errs, the other can remind her.
And let the witnesses not refuse when they are called.
And do not be weary to write it, whether small or large, for its term.
That is more equitable in the sight of Allah and more suitable for evidence and less likely to cause doubt.
Except if it is a present-day trade transaction which you conduct among yourselves, then there is no blame upon you if you do not write it.
And call witnesses when you transact.
And let neither the scribe nor the witness be harmed.
And if you do [harm them], then indeed it is disobedience on your part.
And Allah will teach you. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic legal requirements for recording a debt transaction?
ai.summary: Known as the 'Verse of Debt' (Āyat al-Dayn), this longest verse in the Quran establishes the foundational principles of commercial law, emphasizing the obligation of written contracts to preserve rights and prevent doubt (tarāb). Shia jurisprudence highlights the distinction between the mandatory nature of writing for fixed-term debts and the permissibility of unwritten spot transactions, while also detailing the evidentiary weight of one or two witnesses based on gender and reliability. The verse concludes by linking legal precision to divine knowledge, reinforcing that adherence to these procedural safeguards is an act of piety and a means of avoiding future disputes.
